issues.legal_issue: Credible testimony from related eyewitnesses can support a conviction when their evidence is carefully scrutinised.
material_facts: Six witnesses claimed to have seen the incident, including three injured eyewitnesses.
The eyewitnesses were related to the deceased, but their presence and credibility were not undermined in cross-examination.
The courts below examined their evidence with greater caution and deeper scrutiny.
issues.conclusion: The conviction could rest on the credible eyewitness testimony even though the witnesses were related to the deceased.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the principle that related or interested witnesses’ evidence is not to be rejected solely because of their relationship; it must be assessed with greater caution and deeper scrutiny. The presence of injured eyewitnesses is a weighty indication that they were at the scene. No provision or earlier case was cited for this principle.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and eyewitnesses_were_related and injured_eyewitnesses_were_present and testimony_survived_careful_scrutiny

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The matter is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.eyewitnesses_were_related: The witnesses who described seeing the incident were related to the deceased.
predicates.injured_eyewitnesses_were_present: One or more witnesses who described seeing the incident had also been injured in it.
predicates.testimony_survived_careful_scrutiny: The witnesses’ accounts remained credible after careful examination.

issues.definition: When a conviction appeal involves related eyewitnesses, injured eyewitnesses were present, and their accounts remain credible after careful scrutiny, the conviction may rest on that testimony.

issues.legal_issue: The prosecution’s failure to examine independent witnesses does not undermine a conviction when no independent persons at the scene or resulting prejudice are shown.
material_facts: The defence argued that the prosecution had not examined independent witnesses.
The defence had not established that independent persons were present at the scene.
The defence did not show how the non-examination caused prejudice to the appellants.
issues.conclusion: The non-examination of independent witnesses did not undermine the conviction in these circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed the claimed omission by considering whether independent witnesses were shown to have been available and whether their absence caused prejudice. No provision or earlier case was cited for this assessment.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The matter is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.no_independent_observers_shown_present: The defence did not establish that independent persons were present at the scene.
predicates.no_prejudice_from_non_examination_shown: The defence did not show that the absence of testimony from independent witnesses caused prejudice.

issues.definition: In a conviction appeal, when no independent observers are shown to have been present and no prejudice from their non-examination is shown, their non-examination does not undermine the conviction.

issues.legal_issue: A vague disclosure of an alleged earlier police report does not justify an adverse inference that the prosecution suppressed an earlier account of the incident.
material_facts: The investigating officer said that a village watchman had first reported the occurrence and that a station diary entry was made, but the defence did not elicit the entry’s number, date, or time, or the watchman’s name.
The defence did not seek production of the station diary entry.
The investigating officer stated that the informant’s account was recorded in the case diary in the sequence in which events occurred.
issues.conclusion: No adverse inference could be drawn that the prosecution had suppressed an earlier version of the occurrence.
issues.legal_principle: The court considered that the alleged earlier information was not identified with sufficient particulars, had not been sought for production, and was not shown to contain an earlier version inconsistent with the informant’s account. It cited no provision or earlier case for this conclusion.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and alleged_initial_report_was_vague and station_record_was_not_sought and informant_account_was_recorded_in_sequence

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The matter is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.alleged_initial_report_was_vague: The defence disclosed an alleged initial report without establishing its identifying details or its contents as an earlier account of the incident.
predicates.station_record_was_not_sought: The defence did not seek production of the police station record said to contain the initial information.
predicates.informant_account_was_recorded_in_sequen: The investigating officer stated that the informant’s account was recorded in the case diary in the sequence in which events occurred.

issues.definition: In a conviction appeal, when the alleged initial report is vague, the station record is not sought, and the informant’s account is recorded in sequence, no adverse inference of a suppressed earlier account is drawn.

issues.legal_issue: A distance stated between the scene and a police station does not undermine eyewitness identification when it does not establish the distance from which the witnesses observed the incident.
material_facts: The first information report recorded that the scene was about 300 yards from the police station.
The defence argued that witnesses could not clearly see and identify the assailants from that distance.
The record did not state that the eyewitnesses had observed the incident from a point 300 yards away; counsel accepted that the argument misconstrued the recorded distance.
issues.conclusion: The stated distance did not undermine the eyewitnesses’ ability to observe and identify the assailants.
issues.legal_principle: The court construed the recorded distance according to what it described: the distance between the scene and the police station, not the witnesses’ viewing distance. No provision or earlier case was cited for this conclusion.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The matter is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.recorded_distance_was_to_police_station: The recorded distance described how far the scene was from the police station.
predicates.witnesses_not_shown_to_observe_from_that: The evidence did not show that the eyewitnesses viewed the incident from the recorded distance.

issues.definition: In a conviction appeal, when a recorded distance is to the police station and the witnesses are not shown to have observed the incident from that distance, the distance does not discredit their identification.
